replies.speaker: Haley
replies.text:

line: Prince Forre, what did your runner just tell you? And Your Majesty, how far east has the line slipped?

replies.speaker: Forre
replies.text:
Forre's head tilts, and he doesn't look up from the map. "A messenger's duty is to deliver news, not to explain it." His emerald eyes are fixed on the black token.
He traces the line of the token's new position with a fingertip, and doesn't smile. "The runner says the western front has moved. That's all."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."

replies.speaker: Alexander

"The line has not slipped," he says, and his voice is low. "The line is where I say it is."
He looks at Forre, and his eyes are dark. "You will not tell me we are losing the war."
The King stands, his white fur mantle shifting, and the air in the room is cold. "The line will hold at Fort Vicinitas."
He looks at the party. "And this is why you will go to Greywater. To find the missing dead."
A beat, and his face hardens. "And to end this rumour."

context.text: Prince Forre, what did your runner just tell you? And Your Majesty, how far east has the line slipped?

context.name: Forre
context.text:
Forre's head tilts, and he doesn't look up from the map. "A messenger's duty is to deliver news, not to explain it." His emerald eyes are fixed on the black token.
He traces the line of the token's new position with a fingertip, and doesn't smile. "The runner says the western front has moved. That's all."
He looks up, and his expression is cool. "The line has slipped a mile and a half. A mile and a half that costs us ten villages."
He turns to the King, and his voice is sharp. "Father. We're losing the war."

context.name: Alexander
context.text:
Alexander does not move. His hand rests on the table, and his face is stone.
"The line has not slipped," he says, and his voice is low. "The line is where I say it is."
He looks at Forre, and his eyes are dark. "You will not tell me we are losing the war."
The King stands, his white fur mantle shifting, and the air in the room is cold. "The line will hold at Fort Vicinitas."
He looks at the party. "And this is why you will go to Greywater. To find the missing dead."
A beat, and his face hardens. "And to end this rumour."

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Belle, what do you make of Greywater? ...Actually, never mind. Dalan, how many arrows do we have left?

context.name: Dalan
context.text:
Dalan blinks, his eyes flicking from Belle to Max, then he's counting. "Forty-eight. Thirty-six standard, twelve for piercing." He checks his quiver, then glances at the map. "Not enough to fight our way out of an army."
He looks up at Max, and his cheeks go pink. "But enough to hunt one or two monsters."

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Queen Melisande, will you speak for yourself on this?

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text:
The question is aimed at an empty chair. Melisande's seat is a throne of carved stone, draped in purple velvet and embroidered with the sigils of the Third Kingdom. It sits untouched.
The King's face is stone. Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Princess Haley's grip on her fan tightens until her knuckles are white.
The room is silent, save for the soft crackle of the fire and the creak of a banner in the breeze.

context.name: Haley
context.text:
Haley's fan snaps shut with a sound like a bone breaking. "Mother is not—" She stops, her breath sharp. Her eyes are wide and green, and they're fixed on the empty chair.
"She is not here." Her voice is a thin edge. "And she is not—"
A beat. "She is not necromancer."
Forre's eyes are still on the map. The King's face does not change.
Haley's chin rises, and her fan is open again, this time held like a shield. "And she is not to be spoken of like that."
